DEPARTMENT OF ASSAMESE
BRIEF HISTORY
The Department of Assamese is one of the prestigious departments of the College. Being founded as early as the establishment of the College in 1943, in its glorious journey, the Department was served by some very prominent personalities of Assam like Mr. Jogesh Das, Dr Nirmal Prova Bordoloi, Mr. Bhagagiri Raychoudhury, Dr. Pramod Chandra Bhattacharyya, Mr. Bisweswar Hazarika, Mrs. Pravina Saikia, and Dr Arunima Bharali. All have tremendous contributions to Assamâ€™s literary-cultural world. The former two have achieved Indian Sahitya Akademi Award for their creative writings and were honoured with the post of President of Asam Sahitya Sabha, the foremost literary platform of Assam.
The Department can boast of good academic results, as well as praiseworthy performance in extra-curricular activities. The students are always enthusiastic enough to participate in all activities around the Annual College Week programme, Studentsâ€™ Union Body, NSS, NCC, Community Works, Seminar, Debating, and other literary-cultural activities.
The Department publishes an annual research journal à¦†à¦²à§‹à¦• (Alok) https://www.alokassamese.com in Assamese. Dapon, a Wall Magazine (In early years it was named as Hemahar), Puberun, a Printed Magazine and Unmilan, a manuscript magazine is published by the Department. A literary-cultural forum Sadhana, initiated by the Department provides the students a platform to organize literary -cultural activities, exchange opinions among them on social issues, and meet each other. Pratyahik, a daily page on tabloid form is also run by the students of the Department. The Department organizes a Lecture Programme annually. The Department has a small cultural museum to showcase the diverse cultural traditions of Assam. The Department also has an art and craft gallery, to reflect and expose the creativity of the students.
FACULTY MEMBERS
The Department currently has six permanent posts. Faculties are dynamic, industrious and dedicated. A friendly and cooperative relationship among the teachers and students is a distinctive feature of the Department.
1. Dr. Birinchi Kumar Kalita, MA, Ph D, Associate Professor (Literature)
2. Dr. Indu Prava Devi, MA (Assamese), MA (Nepali), NET, M Phil, Ph D, Associate Professor (Language) and Head.
3. Dr. Gitashree Tamuly, MA (Assamese), MA (English), NET, Ph D, Associate Professor (Language)
4. Dr. Gitanjali Das, MA, NET, M Phil, Ph D, Assistant Professor (Literature)
5. Dr. Utpala Das, MA, NET, M Phil, Ph D, Assistant Professor (Language & Literature)

LIBRARY
Apart from the Central library of the College (Hem Baruah Library), the Department has its own library with about 1500 books on diverse topics. Considering the fact that most students of the Department come from lower income groups, a Book Bank, in addition to the Departmental library, is formed to lend books to needy students. They may borrow books and keep them for the whole semester. The Family of Dr Anu Rani Devi, a faculty of the Department, has donated substantial numbers of books to the Departmental library, in memory of her.
RESEARCH
Being an Undergraduate Department, the Assamese Department has scope to carry out some field-study based research projects under the University curriculum, which provide the students basic knowledge on methodology of research and develop aptitude for research in them. Moreover, the Department always inspires the students to undertake minor research projects funded by the College and other agencies.
Dr Indu Prava Devi, is a recognised Ph.D. guide of Gauhati University.
The Department, after availing the autonomous status of the College, has introduced its PhD program in January 2026. Presently, Four scholars have been pursuing their studies in this program.
MISSION AND VISION
Mission
The mission of the Department is to develop interests in Assamese language, literature and culture, which are core to the lives of most of the people of Assam. The students, with exposure to new ideas and enriched with new ways of knowledge and outlook in the Department, can see and explore novel experience and interpretation in familiar things. The Department aims to build future cultural leaders and creative writers, and tries to broaden the minds of the students with deeper human values and understanding, as well as the respect and commitment for indigenous cultural traditions. The students develop a refined sense of art and culture, become ready to struggle with hurdles of life, and employ their talents, skills and knowledge for the well-being of the nation and humanity.
Vision
The Department is committed to provide the quality education to the students that is possible in a public college of India, to promote their tastes and capabilities, and to widen their mental horizon, as well as to enrich them personally, intellectually, and socially.
